references.text: Isaiah 55:2-4 calls the people to listen and come to water and bread, promises that they shall live forever, and notes that God has appointed the Messiah as a 'witness' (a parallel to sealing), a direct parallel to Jesus' call to work for bread that lasts into eternal life.
John 3:33-34 describes how God has set his seal on the Son's testimony, and that the Son's words are God's words, a direct theological link to the Father's sealing in 6:27.
In the same chapter, Jesus confirms that the Father wants the Son to keep all that is given him, and that he shall give eternal life, which expands on the role given by the Father in 6:27.
Jesus identifies himself as 'the living bread' coming down from heaven, as a direct response to the call to work for the bread that lasts into eternal life.
Jesus explains that whoever eats of the bread shall live forever, and that he lives because of the Father, a direct consequence of the eternal nourishment mentioned in 6:27.
